reader.requirement: At --std 85 an indexed file (whose FD can carry no CODE-SET clause) keeps its data on the external medium in the native character set: every native character a record holds is written without conversion and is read back as the same native character, whatever its ordinal.
reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion|Edition|DialectBehavior over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO (only DialectBehavior gates on READ PREVIOUS, duplicate-key status, sharing, relative WRITE, CLOSE WITH LOCK; none on the medium encoding); FileCharacterSet and StorageByte take no edition; FileDescriptionFormats.Rows (CODE-SET not admitted in Format 2) is edition-invariant.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf03_07 round-trips ordinals 1, 33, 58, 66, 123, 234 and HIGH-VALUE (65536); not covered: native ordinal 256 (U+00FF), which shares the medium byte 0xFF with HIGH-VALUE, and every native character above ordinal 256, which the WRITE refuses

probes.printed: ordinals 200, 129, 1 (LOW-VALUE), 65536 (HIGH-VALUE), 'x' 121, '~' 127 round-trip through WRITE, START, READ NEXT, REWRITE and READ by an alternate key; the character of ordinal 256 written at position 5 and by the REWRITE at position 10 reads back as 65536
probes.expected: each native character reads back unchanged (ordinal 256 stays 256)

probes.printed: WRITTEN ORD=00256 / W1=00 / W2=91 / READ=00 ORD=65536 / READ BACK AS HIGH-VALUE
probes.expected: WRITE of ordinals 256 and 257 succeed (00) and READ returns ORD=00256

probes.printed: control without a file: ORD of C255/C256/C257/HIGH-VALUE = 255/256/257/65536
probes.expected: the native set holds ordinals 1..65536, so ordinal 256 and HIGH-VALUE are distinct native characters

probes.printed: indexed WRITE of ordinals 255,256,257,1001,65535,HIGH-VALUE: WX=91 (refused); relative and sequential files: ordinal 256 reads back as 65536
probes.expected: native characters written to the medium unconverted

probes.printed: error COBOL2604: the CODE-SET clause (CODE-SET IS EBC) is not a clause of Format 2 (relative-or-indexed) of the file description entry
probes.expected: no CODE-SET on an indexed FD at 1985 (the native set is the only one), so the clause is refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR2  (2.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The implementor's native character set is the UTF-16 BMP (DOC-A.1-31; ORD(HIGH-VALUE)=65536, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS up to 65535 accepted), but a fixed-record file's medium is ISO/IEC 8859-1 under the storage-byte law: U+00FF (ordinal 256) and HIGH-VALUE share byte 0xFF, so a written ordinal-256 character reads back as HIGH-VALUE, and any character above U+00FF makes WRITE/REWRITE fail with '91'. The data on the medium is therefore a 256-character projection of the native set, not the native set the rule assumes. This is the owner-accepted cost recorded in kb/Work R52 and R47 (DOC-A.1-31); the orchestrator should weigh the verdict against those decisions.
reader.harm: wrong-answer (ordinal 256 silently reads back as HIGH-VALUE); rejects valid data at run time (native characters above ordinal 256 refused with status 91)
reader.at-2023: identical: WRITTEN ORD=00256 / W1=00 / W2=91 / READ=00 ORD=65536 / READ BACK AS HIGH-VALUE
reader.expected: §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR2 "The native character set is assumed for data on the external media.": W1=00, W2=00, READ=00 ORD=00256, and DX not equal to HIGH-VALUE
reader.observed: W1=00 / W2=91 / READ=00 ORD=65536 / READ BACK AS HIGH-VALUE
reader.known_note: kb/Work R52 (owner decision: HIGH-VALUE U+FFFF, byte 0xFF on a byte medium; accepted cost that U+00FF returns as HIGH-VALUE), kb/Work R47 (owner decision: Latin-1 medium, characters above U+00FF refused), kb/Work PB1759, PB690; docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-31.md

adjudication.reason: The behaviour (a character above U+00FF refused with 91; U+00FF read back as HIGH-VALUE) is fixed by the owner's decisions R47 and R52 and documented in `docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-31.md`; the code does what was decided. Lead: that entry does not state one consequence the checker measured, that two keys differing only in U+00FF against HIGH-VALUE collide (status 21 on a sequential WRITE, 22 on a random one). The rows close on the documented determination, not on a plain CONFORMS.
